subject.title: Telegram agent: chatbot follow-up loop + exec tool aborts on pkill against earlier-spawned process

question: Should this mixed issue be split into canonical follow-up policy work and a separate exec/process-control task, and should raw shell pkill patterns be guarded or only steered toward process kill?
rationale: The follow-up half overlaps with a product-policy reply invariant, while the exec half needs a lower-level process-control decision that source inspection cannot safely choose automatically.

options.title: Split And Scope Separately
options.body: Keep #58450 as the canonical follow-up-policy tracker and create or retain a narrower process-control task for pkill/process kill proof.

options.title: Keep One Coordinated Tracker
options.body: Use this issue to require one combined fix and proof plan across Telegram reply policy and exec process termination.

options.title: Close Follow-Up As Duplicate Only
options.body: Treat only the follow-up half as covered by #58450 and require a fresh standalone exec report before process work proceeds.

recommendation.title: Split And Scope Separately
recommendation.body: Keep #58450 as the canonical follow-up-policy tracker and create or retain a narrower process-control task for pkill/process kill proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has recent history in both auto-reply/embedded-runner follow-through and review routing for this issue family.
